description: Session-continuation token minting (avalon_protocol::continuation). A ContinuationToken is a short-lived, self-signed assertion an already-logged-in identity mints locally so it can keep working against a *different* node than the one that issued its opaque session token, wire-encoded as 'AVCT1.<base64url(json)>' straight into an Authorization: Bearer header. This is the primitive automatic reconnect-on-401 behavior is built on.

notSupported.rust: the Rust SDK (languages/rust) has no client-side ContinuationToken minting at all — avalon_protocol::continuation::signing_bytes exists (server-side verification only, crates/server/src/continuation.rs), but nothing in the Rust SDK calls it. A caller of the Rust SDK that needs cross-node reconnect today has no way to get one. Real gap, not just untested.
notSupported.csharp: languages/csharp/AvalonSdk has no ContinuationToken type or minting code at all, and no automatic reconnect-on-401 behavior anywhere in the project. Real gap, not just untested.
